beats.text: The waterfall model runs the phases in order. Each phase is done once, and the next starts only when the previous one is complete.
It is simple, easy to manage, and it works well for small projects whose requirements are well understood.
But every requirement must be known up front. And major problems are found late, in testing.
There is no parallelism, so people sit idle, waiting for others.
The fix is iterative development. Build a part, test it, get feedback, then build more. Each iteration does some analysis, some design, some coding, and some testing.
Iterations can even run in parallel, with separate teams.
Agile is a highly iterative process. Its purpose: speed up development, and respond to change.
Agile values individuals and interactions over processes and tools. And working software over comprehensive documentation.
Customer collaboration over contract negotiation. And responding to change over following a plan.
Every iteration produces working software. So the customer can see the project, and give better requirements.
The risks: agile is problematic for very small and very large projects, and documentation takes second place.
